# Eric Pargac Biography

Eric Pargac is an actor and filmmaker based in Los Angeles. His recent stage work includes performances at Artists Repertory Theatre in Portland, the IRT Theatre in New York, and Dixon Place. He appeared in the HBO series *Succession* and *The Late Show with Stephen Colbert*.

He serves as a founding artistic director of Furious Theatre Company in Los Angeles, where he has originated multiple roles and received recognition including the Pasadena Arts Council's Gold Crown Award. His theatrical performances have earned accolades such as the 2007 Actor of the Year award from *Stage Scene LA* for his work in *An Impending Rupture of the Belly*.

Beyond acting, Eric has performed improv at iO West in Los Angeles and co-founded the improv group Freudian Slip at Texas A&M University. He has appeared in web series including *The Digressions*, which he also co-directed and produced, as well as *Lost Angeles* and national commercials.

As a filmmaker, Eric received official artist recognition at the New York Television Festival in 2014 and 2015, and qualified as a finalist in the A&E Unscripted Development Pipeline in 2014.

# Eric Pargac - Full Bio

Eric Pargac is an actor, producer, and writer who has performed at Artists Repertory Theatre in productions including "Magellanica Audio Drama," "1984," and "Magellanica."

Before joining Artists Rep, he appeared on New York stages at the IRT Theatre as Seymour in "The Koan of Seymour" and at Dixon Place as Aeneas in "Dido and Aeneas." He also starred in, co-directed, and produced the web series "The Digressions."

Pargac is a co-founder of the critically-acclaimed Furious Theatre Company in Los Angeles, where he served as Co-Artistic Director from 2001-2010. He received the Pasadena Arts Council's Gold Crown Award and the Debut Award from Back Stage West. At Furious, he originated roles including Bill in "Canned Peaches in Syrup" and Clay in "An Impending Rupture of the Belly" (2007 Actor of the Year – Stage Scene LA). Regionally, he played Julie Gordon in "Paradise Lost" at the Tony Award-winning Intiman Theatre in Seattle and Don Weston in the short film "Fifths."

His improvisation experience includes performing at ImprovOlympic in Los Angeles on the house team Glass Onion and co-founding Freudian Slip at Texas A&M University.

Television credits include HBO's "Succession" and "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert," plus the web series "Lost Angeles" and the USC sitcom "God Help Us."

As a filmmaker, he was named an Official Artist of the New York Television Festival in 2014 and 2015, and qualified as a finalist in the A&E Unscripted Development Pipeline and semifinalist for History Channel's Unscripted Development Pipeline.

He holds membership in Actors Equity Association and SAG-AFTRA.

Biography
Jamal Dennis is a professional actor based in Los Angeles, California.

This working actor recently studied at RADA, and he has been studying with Craig Archibald and Lesly Kahn. Meanwhile, he also loves to stay busy and immerse himself in the theatre scene and beyond. He has also done some screen work, including the lead role on the show "Be Someone".

In addition to being able to portray a broad range of characters, Jamal brings a lot of action and physicality to his roles, as he is a black belt in martial arts and weapons training. His styles include Kyokushin, Wu-Shu, Ninjitsu, and Shotokan, and he continues to deepen his familiarity with combat and stunts.

To add to his versatility, Jamal has honed his craft with various accents, bringing characters to life in an authentic way in every aspect of his performance. He is always keen on improvising and letting loose when the situation calls for it! When not in LA, Jamal spends time in Atlanta and New Orleans, and he matches his love of acting and performing with a passion for wellness and physical fitness.

If that wasn't enough Jamal is also a loving father and he enjoys spending quality time with his family.

Follow Jamal on Instagram @theejamaldennis to stay tuned for his next project!

Biography
Eric Pargac is an actor, editor, producer and director who grew up in Texas. He was a founding artistic director of the critically acclaimed Furious Theatre Company in Los Angeles--named one of the Best Theatre Company's of the decade by LA Weekly. At Furious, he starred in 10 productions and received the Pasadena Arts Council's Gold Crown Award and the Debut Award from Back Stage West. He's also done theatre in New York, Portland and Seattle.

Eric starred as Theo in all three seasons of the award-winning web series The Digressions, which he also co-produced and co-directed. He also starred in the web series Lost Angeles. Eric began his career as an improviser, and performed on a house team at ImprovOlympic in Los Angeles.

As a filmmaker, Eric was named as an Official Artist of the New York Television Festival in 2014 and 2015, qualifying as a finalist in the A&E Unscripted Development Pipeline in 2014 and as a semifinalist for History Channel's Unscripted Development Pipeline in 2015.
